title: CurriculumGPT: Supporting Curriculum Design with AI-Augmented Tooling
Evaluating RAG Performance on Small Language Models for Low-Resource Devices through Chunking and Retrieval Methods
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines generative capabilities of language models with external document retrieval to answer questions grounded in reference texts. However, deploying RAG on low-resource devices like Android smartphones is challenging because SLMs have limited computational capacity and depend heavily on efficient chunking and retrieval. Although interest in on-device processing is growing, research on RAG configurations for SLMs under strict resource constraints especially for domain-specific tasks remains limited. This study therefore investigates which combinations of chunking technique, chunk size, overlap, and retrieval strategy best balance accuracy and speed on low-resource devices. The evaluation uses 148 Indonesian questions sourced from an official Hajj guidebook. The study consists of two phases retrieval and generation. Retrieval is evaluated using BLEU, ROUGE-L, MRR, MAP, and Hit@k, while answer quality is measured with BERTScore. The experiments compare different chunking methods (fixed-size or semantic), chunk sizes (128 or 256 tokens), overlaps (25, 50 and 100 tokens), and retrieval methods (dense, sparse, or hybrid). Results show that sparse retrieval with 256-token chunks and 100-token overlap yields the best answer quality (F1 = 0.726). However, 128-token chunks with the same overlap provide the fastest generation time (69.737 seconds). The main contribution of this study is a systematic evaluation of RAG configurations for fully on-device SLMs using a domain-specific Hajj and Umrah dataset not explored in prior research. The findings provide practical guidance for designing efficient and accurate RAG-based question-answering systems on low-resource devices.

title: Essence Coach: A Bot for Software Practice Adoption
abstract: Although Essence has been proposed as a unifying framework for understanding and evaluating software engineering practices, its adoption remains challenging, calling for tools that can act as coaches for learners and practitioners. We present Essence Coach, a chatbot that integrates LLMs with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) from a curated Essence knowledge base. Experiments with multiple LLMs show that RAG consistently improves response quality for Essence-related queries. Some preliminary tests suggest that such systems can help both technical and non-technical students understand and apply Essence concepts. While validation through broader user studies is needed, this work-in-progress highlights how LLMs can bridge abstract SE frameworks and practice adoption.

title: Exploring Agentic RAG for Metadata Question Answering in Enterprise Data Models
abstract: Abstract This paper explores the design and cost-performance trade-offs of agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architectures for metadata question answering (QA) over structured enterprise data models. While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in interpreting structured metadata, their practical deployment is constrained by context window limitations, token costs, and limited transparency in reasoning processes. To address these challenges, we investigate an agentic RAG framework that decomposes metadata QA into multiple coordinated steps, combining category-specific retrieval with a multi-agent architecture operating on declarative data model definitions. Rather than aiming to outperform existing approaches, the proposed system is designed to investigate how modular decomposition and selective retrieval influence token consumption and answer quality. We evaluate the approach against a standalone LLM baseline using a controlled question catalog with varying levels of reasoning complexity. The results indicate that the agentic system reduces input token consumption by approximately 33% on average, while maintaining comparable answer completeness. At the same time, completion token usage increases due to coordination overhead, highlighting a structural trade-off between input efficiency and generation cost. Further analysis indicates that token consumption scales primarily with the number of reasoning steps and the volume of retrieved context, suggesting that the performance of agentic RAG depends strongly on query complexity. These findings provide empirical insights into the design space of agentic LLM systems and contribute to a better understanding of when modular, RAG-based architectures may be beneficial for enterprise metadata analysis.

title: Storyline Trees: Hierarchical Representations for Long-Form Narratives
abstract: Long-form narratives are challenging for longcontext models because their structure is implicit: events, characters, and plotlines interact across hundreds of pages without the explicit cues that guide navigation in structured documents.We address this by constructing storyline trees, hierarchical representations that organize narratives from global themes and major plotlines to fine-grained events.We first segment chapters into contiguous narrative segments, or scenes, and use them as the basic units for tree construction.We then infer storyline trees through complementary top-down and bottom-up procedures that derive, refine, cluster, and summarize storylines at multiple levels of abstraction.We showcase the utility of this representation for question answering: storyline trees enable adaptive retrieval, allowing models to iteratively inspect high-level narrative structure and retrieve scene-level evidence on demand.Experiments on three long-context narrative QA benchmarks show that adaptive retrieval outperforms strong baselines, including post-trained long-context models and agentic chunk-based methods.Ablations confirm that scenes are more effective basic units than chapters or generic segmentation, and that gains persist under matched retrieval budgets 1 .
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP (Findings of EMNLP)

title: Data validation: SOC and LLM approaches
abstract: Data validation has evolved from a static preprocessing step into a continuous requirement in modern AI-driven systems operating in high-volume and adversarial environments. This paper analyzes validation challenges across two domains: Security Operations Centers (SOC) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines. While traditional validation focuses on structural correctness and consistency, SOC and RAG systems require additional guarantees related to semantic integrity, temporal validity, and resilience against adversarial manipulation.Based on a structured analysis of recent approaches, we identify common validation patterns across these domains and highlight the increasing role of AI-assisted techniques, LLM-based reasoning, multi-agent validation, and reliability-aware retrieval. To support this analysis, we provide a comparative overview of existing validation methods, emphasizing their trade-offs in terms of real-time applicability and computational cost.Building on these observations, we outline a conceptual, agent-based validation architecture that integrates structural, semantic, and adversarial validation layers. A feasibility-oriented analysis shows that such systems are most practical as selective and hybrid pipelines, where high-cost LLM-based validation is applied only to high-risk cases. We conclude that data validation should be treated as a multi-layered architectural component essential for ensuring trust and robustness in both AI and security systems.
venue: IEEE International Conference and Workshop Óbuda on Electrical and Power Engineering (CANDO-EPE)

title: Optimizing Low-Parameterised LLMs with RAG using Entropy-based Chunking
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can create an inaccurate or (relevant) response outside of their performance-based conventions, when a long text or poorly constructed text is presented to them. This issue becomes even more serious with smaller models that are less powerful and have limited resources. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, on the other hand, rely on external knowledge to reduce the chances of such errors occurring, but the quality of the retrieval relies heavily on the way the documents are cut up. Poor chunking splits up the meaning of the text, lowers the accuracy of the retrieval and increases the lost-in-the-middle effect, which eventually results in wrong or made-up outputs. This paper aims at a systematic evaluation and exploration of chunking strategies for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems with the small LLMs. We investigate several chunking methods, including fixed-size, semantic and overlapping chunking, and evaluate their influence on retrieval quality, context relevance and hallucination rate. We then come up with and successfully implement an Entropy-Based Chunking method that can automatically detect the areas of the highest information content and create context segments that are joined in meaning but less in number. We carried out our research through empirical analysis of chunking strategies on diverse datasets, assessment of the retrieval behavior using embedding-based search, hallucination measurement applying the existing benchmark techniques, and embedding of our entropy-based chunking within a small-LLM RAG pipeline. Our results clearly show that the retrieval is much more coherent, middle-context is better recalled, and hallucination has been significantly reduced when compared with the standard chunking baseline methods. Instead of increasing the size of the model, this study optimized chunking and thus offered an efficient and accessible application that can be incorporated into real-world scenarios.
venue: International Conference on Inventive Computing and Informatics (ICICI)

title: PIC-Thai: Morphologically-Aware Dynamic Chunking for Semantic Integrity in Thai Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Document chunking is a practical but under-specified design choice in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). This issue is especially important for Thai, where continuous script, weak sentence-boundary cues, and long legal clauses make naive character splitting unreliable. This paper introduces PIC-Thai, a morphologically-aware adaptation of pseudo-instruction-guided document chunking for Thai RAG. PIC-Thai combines Thai-aware atomic splitting, mT5-based pseudo-instruction generation, sentence-to-instruction similarity tracking, and minimum-size post-processing. The evaluation uses 500 Thai legal query–context pairs, adds a 500-pair Thai Wikipedia diagnostic set, compares fallback and no-fallback variants, analyzes threshold and window-size sensitivity, and reports computational cost and bootstrap significance. In the primary legal no-fallback setting (τ = 0.30, w = 8, s = 4), PIC-Thai obtains Recall@3 of 0.664 and MRR@3 of 0.559 with 632 indexed chunks, outperforming the evaluated recursive, token-aware, Thai NLP sentence, and semantic-only baselines in legal-domain Recall@3. Bootstrap testing with 10,000 resamples shows nominally significant Recall@3 improvements on the legal set, although effect sizes are small to modest. On the Thai Wikipedia diagnostic set, fixed-size and Thai NLP baselines remain competitive, indicating that PIC-Thai is useful mainly for structurally complex Thai legal text rather than as a universal chunking replacement.
venue: International Joint Conference on Computer Science and Software Engineering

title: RAG-Based Enterprise Knowledge Platform: Design and Evaluation
Synergistic multi-stage processing for enhanced context relevance in RAG architecture
abstract: In recent years, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have faced critical limitations in semantic consistency, cross-model compatibility, and knowledge-aware response generation. This study introduces SynRAG, an integrated framework designed to overcome these challenges by combining four main innovations: hierarchical semantic segmentation supported by clustering methods, a multi-phase hybrid retrieval mechanism, embedding dimension adjustment strategies, and context-aware prompt engineering. Experimental evaluation on NarrativeQA, QASPER, and QuALITY demonstrates superior performance: on NarrativeQA, the framework achieves 95.3% faithfulness and 96.1% answer relevancy, representing + 11.1 pp and + 21.0 pp improvements respectively; across other datasets, consistent gains are observed on grounding, retrieval (NDCG), and generation metrics. Notably, our dimension transformation maintains high retention relative to 1536-dim embeddings: 95.1% Faithfulness, 94.5% Answer Relevancy, and 93.1% NDCG on average when reduced to 768-dim. Comprehensive evaluation demonstrates consistent improvements across all key metrics, highlighting the robustness of the RAG system. SynRAG marks a notable step forward in RAG development by offering an integrated framework that effectively connects research-level innovations with real-world deployment needs, ensuring both efficiency and scalability in computation.

title: Text Segmentation of City Council Minutes in European Portuguese
abstract: Com a crescente aposta na transparência pública, as câmaras municipais têm vindo a converter os seus arquivos e atas em bases de dados digitais.No entanto, a consulta manual destes documentos continua a ser difícil, pois são textos longos e densos, organizados segundo convenções administrativas que variam entre câmaras.Esta dissertação foca-se na segmentação de texto de atas de câmaras municipais, com o objetivo de dividir automaticamente estes registos em temas ou assuntos coerentes.Estas atas são um desafio para a computação porque são muito extensas, utilizam uma linguagem administrativa específica e nem sempre recorrem a marcadores ou separadores normalizados que indiquem claramente a transição entre assuntos, o que as distingue de outros tipos de texto, como notícias ou artigos científicos.Para resolver este problema, propomos o SegNSP, uma abordagem que dispensa dados anotados com etiquetas semânticas, adaptando o objetivo de pré-treino Next Sentence Prediction para detetar as fronteiras entre tópicos, através da continuidade entre frases adjacentes.A metodologia introduz melhorias significativas face às arquiteturas baseadas em Transformers, designadamente através de rácios de amostragem equilibrados, estratégias de amostragem negativa robusta e uma função de perda dedicada à segmentação.A avaliação do modelo recorre a várias métricas de precisão, nomeadamente P k , WindowDiff (WD), Boundary F β -measure (B-F 1 ) e Boundary Similarity (B), aplicadas a dois conjuntos de dados: o conjunto de referência internacional WikiSection e uma versão adaptada da nova coleção CitiLink-Minutes.Destaca-se a nossa contribuição no desenvolvimento deste último, que constitui a primeira coleção de referência para atas administrativas em português europeu, incluindo 120 documentos manualmente anotados de seis municípios distintos.Os resultados demonstram a eficácia do SegNSP, que estabelece uma base de referência linear competitiva, alcançando um B-F 1 de 79.22 e um B de 59.31 no CitiLink-Minutes, superando vários modelos neuronais e não supervisionados.Para colmatar as limitações da segmentação linear em documentos com estruturas aninhadas, introduzimos de seguida o HSeg, um modelo hierárquico, recursivo e generativo baseado em modelos de linguagem de grande escala (Large Language Models (LLMs)).Avaliado tanto no domínio administrativo como no corpus WIKI-727K, o HSeg supera o estado da arte reportado na literatura.No CitiLink-Minutes, o modelo atinge um B-F 1 de 89.16 na extração de assuntos recorrendo a modelos proprietários de última geração, abrindo também caminho para a validação de alternativas open-weight especializadas.Adicionalmente, no corpus WIKI-727K, demonstra que mesmo LLMs otimizados e mais leves conseguem superar as arquiteturas dedicadas anteriores com uma melhoria absoluta de +9,06 pontos na métrica F 1 (80,66 face a 71,60), com modelos de última geração como o Claude Opus 4.7 a estabelecerem ainda os melhores resultados em termos de P k e precisão.Em última análise, este trabalho procura tornar as atas municipais mais acessíveis e úteis, tanto para funcionários públicos como para cidadãos.
venue: Portuguese National Funding Agency for Science, Research and Technology (RCAAP Project by FCT)

title: Identifying Challenges and Practitioner Techniques in the Use of Verification-Aware Programming Languages
abstract: Garantir a fiabilidade do software tornou-se uma preocupação crescente à medida que os sistemas de software aumentam de complexidade e expandem-se para domínios de sistemas críticos, tais como a saúde, as finanças e a mobilidade.Entre as técnicas desenvolvidas para enfrentar este desafio, a Verificação Formal oferece garantias matemáticas de correção que vão além daquilo que os testes tradicionais conseguem fazer.As linguagens de programação Verification-Aware integram a verificação formal no fluxo de trabalho do desenvolvimento de software, permitindo que os programadores definam especificações em conjunto com o código de implementação, o que possibilita a deteção precoce de erros e garantias de correção mais robustas.Este trabalho centra-se especificamente nas fases de especificação e implementação do desenvolvimento de software, nas quais os programadores escrevem e verificam especificações formais em paralelo com o código, em vez de se focar nas atividades iniciais de planeamento ou definição de requisitos.Apesar destas vantagens, a adoção de linguagens de verificação continua a ser limitada.Os profissionais enfrentam grandes desafios ao trabalhar com estas ferramentas, incluindo a dificuldade em construir e fazer o debugging de provas, interpretar mensagens de erro pouco informativas e gerir a sobrecarga cognitiva do raciocínio formal.Embora investigações anteriores tenham começado a documentar estes obstáculos, as estratégias que os programadores utilizam para os ultrapassar não foram ainda exploradas.Este trabalho aborda esta lacuna através da recolha e análise de conteúdos multimédia nos quais os utilizadores interagem diretamente com linguagens Verification-Aware enquanto resolvem problemas de verificação.Ao contrário de estudos anteriores baseados em discussões de texto, este trabalho capta os processos de raciocínio e as práticas dos programadores à medida que surgem.Utilizando um pipeline que combina semantic similarity filtering e topic modeling, extraímos uma taxonomia de técnicas de verificação, organizada em categorias temáticas.O conjunto de técnicas resultante foi validado através de um questionário que incluiu participantes com experiência em verificação formal, avaliando a sua frequência, complexidade e aplicabilidade.Os resultados da validação revelam práticas comuns de verificação e as técnicas mais frequentemente adotadas pelos programadores, identificando áreas onde continuam a sentir dificuldades significativas.Estes resultados fornecem evidência sobre o workflow de verificação na prática e sugerem perspetivas que têm o potencial de apoiar o design de ferramentas mais utilizáveis, recursos educativos e investigação futura em verificação formal.
venue: Portuguese National Funding Agency for Science, Research and Technology (RCAAP Project by FCT)

title: Can Retrievers Find the Same Paper from Different Aspects? A Multi-Aspect Full-Paper Scientific Retrieval Benchmark
abstract: Scientific papers contain multiple searchable facets such as background, methods. However, many paper retrieval benchmarks merely evaluate individual query-paper relevance, while overlooking other facets of the same paper. To bridge this gap, we introduce MAPLE, an expert-validated benchmark for multi-aspect, full-paper retrieval that evaluates whether retrievers can consistently recover the same paper from queries targeting its motivation, method, and experimental findings. MAPLE contains 2,095 queries about recent ML and NLP papers, grounded in both textual and multimodal content. We further propose MAPLE-Synth, a retrieval-based in-context learning pipeline that leverages OpenReview discussions and human-written query exemplars to generate realistic queries reflecting researchers' interests in different aspects of a paper. Our expert validation shows that these queries are comparable in realism to human-written queries and highly relevant to the target papers. Experiments across lexical, scientific-domain, general-purpose text, and multimodal retrievers reveal a substantial gap between retrieving a paper from any one aspect and retrieving it from all aspects: the strongest model achieves 98.1% AnyAspect@20 but only 15.7% AllAspect@20. Experiment/result queries and table-referenced queries are particularly difficult across retrievers. Although multi-chunk aggregation improves multi-aspect paper retrieval, considerable failures persist. MAPLE provides a testbed for evaluating and developing retrievers that represent scientific papers more comprehensively.

title: Large language models (LLMs) for legal analysis: RAG and beyond for optimizing domain adaptation in Portuguese legal domain
abstract: This study explores RAG systems tailored to the Portuguese legal domain, highlighting challenges in underrepresented languages. Fixed-size chunking strategies, particularly Token Text Splitter, were found to be most effective, while more advanced techniques like Recursive and Semantic splitting showed little benefits. Larger chunk sizes improved retrieval accuracy and answer quality, though the impact of chunk overlap remains inconclusive. Self-reflection techniques show promising results, particularly for weaker LLMs. Techniques such as adding a pre-post translation proved to be an efficient technique for mitigating language bias.
venue: Portuguese National Funding Agency for Science, Research and Technology (RCAAP Project by FCT)

title: Large language models (LLMS) for legal analysis rag and beyond for optimizing domain adaptation in Portuguese legal domain-advanced retrieval and prompt engineering techniques for retrieval augmented generation in the Portuguese legal domain
abstract: This study explores RAG systems tailored to the Portuguese legal domain, highlighting challenges in underrepresented languages. Fixed-size chunking strategies, particularly Token Text Splitter, were found to be most effective, while more advanced techniques like Recursive and Semantic splitting showed little benefits. Larger chunk sizes improved retrieval accuracy and answer quality, though the impact of chunk overlap remains inconclusive. Self reflection techniques show promising results, particularly for weaker LLMs. GraphRAG shows promise with faster results than traditional RAG approaches. Reranking techniques can improve retrieval but require larger, diverse datasets. Reasoning-based and zero-shot prompting improve accuracy in multi-hop scenarios. Pre-post translation proved to be an efficient technique for mitigating language bias.
venue: Portuguese National Funding Agency for Science, Research and Technology (RCAAP Project by FCT)

title: SmartCLAI: A Unified Multi-Agent CLI for Automated Network Configuration
abstract: Managing modern multi-vendor networks remains a major challenge due to diverse device operating systems and inconsistent command-line interfaces (CLIs). Manual configuration is slow and error-prone, limiting automation and intent-based management. To address this challenge, we propose SmartCLAI, an intelligent network automation framework that applies large language models (LLMs) to translate natural-language intents into validated, vendor-specific CLI commands. SmartCLAI introduces three key innovations: a Table-of-Contents-based retriever that improves context accuracy, query clustering for decomposing complex multi-topic requests, and a syntax- and rule-based verification layer that ensures correctness before execution. Integrated directly with device CLIs, SmartCLAI enables an end-to-end, trustworthy automation workflow. Experimental evaluations on real-world network configuration tasks on SONiC and Cisco devices show up to 94% configuration accuracy and 42% and 41% lower token cost than baselines. Our results highlight SmartCLAI's potential in intelligent automation of complex configuration tasks in multi-vendor network infrastructures. For the evaluation dataset, see https://mygit.th-deg.de/inets/smartclai/.
venue: IEEE/IFIP Network Operations and Management Symposium (NOMS)

title: A Deterministic Procedure-Aware Bilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Trustworthy High-Stakes AI Systems
abstract: The advent of large language models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models has greatly enhanced intelligent information systems. This has resulted in the development of context-aware and knowledge-grounded response generation. This has been highly beneficial in the context of religious advisory systems, which require precision, correctness, and knowledge grounding. For Islamic rituals like Hajj and Umrah, the user needs precise and accurate procedures to follow, which must adhere to specific sequences and knowledge grounding. However, the existing models have many limitations in this context, like hallucinations, a lack of procedural knowledge, bilingual inconsistencies, and an inability to incorporate safety constraints. This has made these models unsuitable for contexts in which incorrect responses can have serious implications. Therefore, in this context, this paper proposes a Deterministic Procedure-Aware bilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation (DPAM-RAG) model, which can be highly beneficial in designing religious advisory systems. The proposed model can be highly beneficial in designing religious advisory systems. The proposed model integrates dataset modeling, procedure-aware chunking, bilingual alignment, and deterministic transformer-based response generation. Additionally, a confidence-based refusal strategy has been proposed to avoid the generation of responses that can be considered incorrect or out of context. The proposed model has been tested through an extensive experimental setup, which includes multiple transformer models like GPT, LLaMA-2, Mistral, MPT, and BLOOMZ. The experimental results have shown promising outcomes, which can be considered highly beneficial in designing trustworthy AI models.

title: Optimización y segmentación basada en grafos para estrategias de chunking en sistemas Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
abstract: La segmentación documental (chunking) desempeña un papel importante en la recuperación de información dentro de los sistemas Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Las estrategias Fixed Chunking, Sentence Chunking y Semantic Chunking utilizan distintos criterios para dividir los documentos, pero no consideran de forma conjunta las relaciones semánticas y estructurales entre las unidades textuales. En este trabajo se formuló e implementó una estrategia de Graph Chunking basada en teoría de grafos y optimización, y se comparó su comportamiento con las tres estrategias mencionadas. La investigación siguió un enfoque cuantitativo con diseño experimental. Primero se evaluaron nueve configuraciones del método propuesto y se seleccionó la configuración L100_T45_W10 para la comparación posterior. Las pruebas se realizaron sobre documentos de diferente extensión y se utilizaron las mismas consultas, el mismo modelo de embeddings y el mismo índice vectorial. Se consideraron los tiempos de procesamiento y las métricas Hit Rate, Precision, Recall, Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) y Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (nDCG). Graph Chunking obtuvo los valores más altos de Hit Rate y Recall en los tres documentos, además de los mayores valores de MRR y nDCG en los documentos grande y mediano. En el documento pequeño, Semantic Chunking presentó el mayor MRR, mientras que Graph Chunking y Semantic Chunking obtuvieron el mismo valor de nDCG. El método basado en grafos requirió mayor tiempo durante la segmentación, pero registró menores tiempos de recuperación y de generación de embeddings en los documentos analizados. Los resultados muestran que incorporar relaciones semánticas y estructurales durante la construcción de los fragmentos constituye una alternativa para la segmentación documental en sistemas RAG.

title: AN OFFLINE RAG SYSTEM PROTOTYPE FOR SAFE QUERYING OF UNSTRUCTURED DOCUMENTS
abstract: In the context of large language models (LLMs) being utilized within organizations that manage sensitive data, two notable limitations of commercial cloud solutions become evident.Firstly, there is the risk of confidential information being disclosed when content is transmitted to external servers.Secondly, there is the issue of the models' propensity to hallucinate in the absence of reliable context.The present paper proposes and implements a prototype of a fully offline RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) system using exclusively open-source components.The architecture is predicated on the Agentic RAG approach, which substitutes linear query processing with a multi-agent system orchestrated using the LangGraph framework.A hybrid (dense + sparse) approach over the Qdrant vector database is used for search, and the parallel relational database DuckDB is used for tabular data.The system is containerized using Docker Compose and runs a local LLM via the Ollama platform.The evaluation of the output quality was conducted through a comparative analysis with three existing tools (LM Studio, AnythingLLM, NotebookLM) on a set of ten extensive PDF reports on climate change.The evaluation process involved the utilization of five complex questions, necessitating the synthesis of information from multiple sources.The implemented prototype achieved a level of accuracy comparable to the cloud-based NotebookLM tool and significantly outperformed solutions employing local LLMs.It also maintained transparency of answers through citations of source documents and ensured that data remained on the user's local device.
venue: International Conference Economic Competitiveness and Sustainability

title: Agentic retrieval-augmented generation framework for exploring Bayesian network literature
abstract: Este trabajo de fin de máster presenta el diseño, la implementación y la evaluación de BN Assistant, un marco de agentic RAG para la exploración de literatura científica sobre redes bayesianas. El crecimiento exponencial de las publicaciones académicas ha hecho que la recuperación y la síntesis efectiva del conocimiento sean cada vez más complejas, especialmente en campos especializados caracterizados por estructuras formales y dependencias complejas. Aunque los LLMs ofrecen potentes capacidades generativas, presentan limitaciones como las alucinaciones y la falta de trazabilidad. Para hacer frente a estos retos, este trabajo propone una arquitectura basada en agentes que amplía los sistemas RAG tradicionales mediante la incorporación de orquestación sensible a la intención, selección dinámica de herramientas y representaciones híbridas del conocimiento. El sistema integra recuperación mediante vectores densos con consultas sobre metadatos estructurados a través de text-to-SQL, lo que permite tanto la comprensión semántica como una trazabilidad bibliográfica precisa. Asimismo, se desarrolla una canalización modular para la ingesta, el preprocesamiento, la segmentación y la generación de embeddings de documentos, con el objetivo de preservar los matices estructurales de la literatura sobre redes bayesianas. El marco resultante, BN Assistant, se evalúa mediante una metodología en varias fases que analiza la precisión de la recuperación, la calidad de la generación, el control de alucinaciones y la toma de decisiones agéntica. Los resultados experimentales demuestran que el enfoque autónomo mejora tanto la fiabilidad como la interpretabilidad de las respuestas generadas a partir de literatura sobre redes bayesianas. En definitiva, este trabajo contribuye al desarrollo de sistemas de inteligencia artificial fiables para la síntesis de conocimiento científico, haciendo hincapié en la verificabilidad, las rutas de recuperación trazables y el razonamiento específico del dominio. --ABSTRACT-- This master’s thesis presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of BN Assistant, an agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework for exploring Bayesian network (BN) literature. The exponential growth of academic publications has made effective knowledge retrieval and synthesis increasingly challenging, particularly in specialized fields characterized by formal structure and complex dependencies. While large language models (LLMs) offer powerful generative capabilities, they suffer from limitations such as hallucinations and lack of traceability. To address these challenges, this work proposes an agent-based architecture that extends traditional RAG systems by incorporating intent-aware orchestration, dynamic tool selection, and hybrid knowledge representations. The system integrates dense vector retrieval with structured metadata querying through text-to-SQL, enabling both semantic understanding and precise bibliographic traceability. A modular pipeline for document ingestion, preprocessing, chunking, and embedding generation is developed to preserve the structural nuances of BN literature. The resulting framework, BN Assistant, is evaluated through a multi-stage methodology assessing retrieval accuracy, generation quality, hallucination control, and agentic decision-making. The experimental results demonstrate that the autonomous approach improves both the reliability and interpretability of responses generated from BN literature. Ultimately, this work contributes to the development of trustworthy artificial intelligence (AI) systems for scientific knowledge synthesis by emphasizing verifiability, traceable retrieval paths, and domain-specific reasoning.
venue: Archivo Digital UPM (Universidad Politécnica de Madrid)

title: Chunk Size and Retrieval Depth Optimization in a Minimal Retrieval-Augmented Generation Pipeline
abstract: Retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG) links a large language model to a set of texts. But RAG works well only when two settings are right: how big each piece of text (a "chunk") is, and how many pieces the model reads. People often choose these by habit, not by data. In this study we tested how both settings change the results of a simple RAG pipeline. We used a closed-domain set of 120 academic-regulation documents (246,800 tokens in total). We cut the documents into chunks of four sizes (128, 256, 512, and 1024 tokens) with 25% overlap, and we also tried one version with no overlap. Each chunk was turned into a vector with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and stored in FAISS with exact inner-product search. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct then answered questions using the retrieved chunks, at retrieval depths k = 1, 3, 5, and 10. We used 200 question-answer pairs: 120 answerable items as a development set (used to choose all settings) and a held-out test set of 60 answerable items plus 20 unanswerable items (used only once). On the development set, retrieval recall was best at 256-token chunks (recall = 0.825 at k = 5), while context precision fell steadily from 0.428 to 0.172 as chunks grew. Answer F1 was highest at k = 5 (71.3) and then dropped to 69.2 at k = 10, even though recall kept rising. Our final configuration was L = 256, O = 64 (25% overlap), k = 5. On the held-out test set this configuration reached an F1 of 70.1. That is 37.5 points higher than a closed-book baseline (p < 0.001) and 8.9 points higher than a BM25 baseline (p = 0.004). Correct abstention on unanswerable questions improved from 15.0% to 70.0%. Manual error analysis showed that 17.9% of the failures were caused by chunk-boundary fragmentation.
venue: International Journal of Innovations in Science and Technology

title: From Source Code to Network Profile: Automated and Traceable MUD Profile Generation for IoT Devices
abstract: The Manufacturer Usage Description (MUD) standard allows IoT manufacturers to define expected network behaviors in a MUD file. This file can be translated into enforceable access-control policies, restricting compromised devices to operate solely through manufacturer-defined communication patterns. However, practical adoption of MUD depends on profiles that are accurate, complete, and maintainable. Existing approaches use traffic-based automation but require device deployment and prolonged monitoring, capturing only behavior exercised during observation. Rare, failure-triggered, or configuration-dependent communications may remain absent, producing incomplete policies that disrupt legitimate operation and offer limited insight into the software components responsible for each rule. We present AutoMUD, a source-code-driven tool that generates traceable MUD profiles for IoT devices from their firmware and software source code. AutoMUD combines static and syntactic extraction, retrieval-grounded language-model reasoning, and deterministic validation and compilation to recover the communication behavior characterizing an IoT device and translate eligible endpoints into policy rules. By analyzing code-level evidence, AutoMUD exposes rarely exercised and conditional communication paths, links every generated rule to its source-level provenance, and preserves excluded findings with explicit reasons for review. Our evaluation on a Linux-based repository demonstrates that AutoMUD recovers complete communication behavior, consolidates validated behavior into semantic endpoint groups, and generates structurally valid MUD profiles. Through a controlled semantic fault-injection campaign, we demonstrate that AutoMUD enables analysts to detect, localize, explain, and correct propagated errors, recovering policies semantically identical to their clean counterparts.

title: Geometric Characterization of Embedding Spaces Across Chunking Strategies and Embedding Models for Slovenian Text
abstract: This paper investigates whether geometric properties of embedding spaces can provide useful intrinsic indicators for evaluating text chunking strategies and embedding models without relying on downstream tasks.We evaluate several text chunking strategies with different overlap configurations using five embedding models on a large collection of historical Slovenian newspapers.Our results show that embedding-space geometry is strongly modeldependent, while chunking strategies substantially affect local continuity, cluster separation, and how well cluster centroids represent the original article.Token-based chunking with approximately 256 tokens and 25% overlap provided the most consistent balance between the evaluated geometric properties and computational requirements.The results also show that no individual geometric metric defines embedding-space quality and that complementary properties should therefore be interpreted jointly.

title: A Neutral and Evidence-Grounded Evaluation of Chunking Strategies in Industrial RAG Systems
Developing AI Enterprise Solutions using Large Language Models and Knowledge Bases
abstract: Magistrsko delo obravnava uporabo velikih jezikovnih modelov v poslovnih okoljih ter predlaga arhitekturo sistema za upravljanje znanja, ki z generiranjem, obogatenim z iskanjem (RAG), omejuje nezanesljive odgovore in izkorišča nestrukturirane interne podatke. Sistem samodejno zajema podatke iz dokumentnih sistemov in komunikacijskih platform ter jih pretvarja v atomarna dejstva in dele dokumentov. Vsebino in metapodatke hrani v relacijski podatkovni bazi, njihove vektorske vložitve pa v ločenih zbirkah vektorske podatkovne baze. Pri prilagodljivem pridobivanju glede na vrsto vprašanja najprej izbere atomarna dejstva ali dele dokumentov, po potrebi pa pridobi še kontekst iz druge zbirke. Pilotno implementacijo smo preverili na sintetičnem korpusu z 32 izvornimi dokumenti, razdeljenimi v štiri časovno zaporedne faze. Sistem je dokumente razdelil na 61 delov in iz njih izluščil 420 atomarnih dejstev. Slepo ročno ovrednotenje je zajelo 64 vprašanj in po en odgovor vsake od štirih strategij pridobivanja ter kontrole brez RAG, skupaj 320 odgovorov. Prilagodljivo pridobivanje, pri katerem agent izbira med dejstvi in deli dokumentov, je doseglo najvišji opaženi skupni rezultat (5,83 od 6,0) in v eni izvedbi merjenja najnižjo mediano pretečenega časa zahteve med strategijami RAG, vendar primerjava ni povsem ločila učinka strategije pridobivanja od razlik v ubeseditvi navodil, pri primarnih merilih pa nismo potrdili statistično značilnih razlik med štirimi strategijami RAG. Pregled vzorca 50 aktivnih dejstev je pokazal visok delež najvišjih ocen atomarnosti, samostojnosti in zvestobe viru, vse tri nadomestitve v končni zbirki pa so bile vsebinsko upravičene. Rezultati podpirajo tehnično izvedljivost v sintetičnem pilotu ter kažejo možen kompromis med kakovostjo, pretečenim časom zahteve in porabo žetonov, za sklep o prednosti, skalabilnosti, varnosti ali produkcijski pripravljenosti pa so potrebni širši in ponovljeni preizkusi.

Granularity is the Hidden Bias: Revisiting the Factual Consistency Evaluation for Summarization
abstract: Factual consistency evaluation for summarization has attracted increasing attention as large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate hallucinations. Existing evaluation methods implicitly obey the fixed-fact-granularity assumation (verifying summaries under a uniform claim segmentation granularity) implicitly when decomposing and verifying summary content. This assumption inevitably introduces a hidden but systematic evaluation bias in real-world scenarios: logically independent facts may be merged to mask errors, while semantically interdependent complex facts may be over-splitting and break relational semantics. We revisit this problem from the perspective of granularity control, revealing that granularity mismatch is a fundamental failure mode that affects the reliability and interpretability of the evaluation. To address this problem, we propose a factual consistency evaluation framework FAIR, which achieves explicit modeling of factual granularity by performing logically aware fact segmentation on the summary and semantically aware evidence segmentation on the source documents. Furthermore, FAIR employs a retrieval-enhanced verification mechanism to perform precise alignment and verification of atomic content units and outputs concrete error types. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that FAIR achieves stronger correlation with human fidelity judgments and reduces evaluation bias, delivering both interpretable and reliable assessment of LLM-based summarization.
venue: International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)

title: Sustainable Local RAG Architectures for Energy Governance: A Green AI Approach via Document Slice Contextualization
abstract: Abstract Background: Retrieval-augmented generation pipelines that contextualize every chunk against its whole document follow a “Red AI” pattern: quadratic self-attention and a linearly growing key–value cache push index-time inference beyond the 8 GB of a consumer GPU, while energy-sector auditing and policy work, bound by data-sovereignty rules, must run locally. Results: We formalize Document Slice contextualization, which conditions each chunk summary on a bounded window of neighboring chunks, and add a two-tier routing agent that selects the radius for each chunk using a regex gate and a single-token forward pass of the same 4B-parameter model. On 25 scientific papers (382 chunks, 250 multi-hop questions) the router chose a mean radius of 1.37, skipped 32 % of the summaries and reached Recall@20 of 0.952 against 0.954 for full-document contextualization, with higher MRR, while cutting tracked generation energy from 106.7 to 13.2 Wh (-87.6 %), emissions from 21.8 to 2.8 gCO2eq and generation time from 54.9 to 8.8 min. In four European Commission policy documents, the fixed-radius variant remained within 0.6 points of the baseline, at 71.8 % lower energy. Conclusions: Bounded, routed contextualization offers a PEP-AI pathway (Precise, Explainable, Provable) to decentralized compliance auditing: reproducible metrics, inspectable per-chunk decisions, and per-run energy ledgers.

title: Twin-AI: A Privacy-Preserving Dual-Memory Architecture for Cognitive Digital Twins via Local Large Language Models
abstract: Most Large Language Models (LLMs) are fundamentally stateless tools. As these models predict on the basis of general statistical distributions, they do not understand the particular coding style, behavioral quirks, and decision rationales of individual developers. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a privacy-preserving Cognitive Digital Twin (CDT) architecture namely Twin-AI. Twin-AI allows you to run highly personalized, autonomous AI agents directly on edge hardware. Based on a novel Dual-Memory Cognitive Architecture, the system separates factual episodic knowledge (stored in a ChromaDB vector store) from behavioral patterns (stored in a SQLite relational database). We introduce T-AST Differencing, a technique that models user behavior without relying on stochastic LLM estimates. This deterministic engine directly learns coding, writing and refactoring traits from version control history. Beside the Four-Factor Confidence Calibration algorithm, we also add a Meta-Cognitive Reflection Loop. These mechanisms work together to verify, before execution, that the generated outputs are consistent with the user’s previous reasoning, in an iterative fashion. Twin-AI was evaluated on a generalized multi-user validation suite containing 1,014 semantic chunks from N = 3 developers, achieving a Syntactic Alignment Score of 0.924±0.012 and an Expected Calibration Error (ECE) of 0.075±0.004 on edge hardware, and showing a measurable improvement over standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation baselines.

title: Knowledge Base-Driven Response Generation for Customer Support Using Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This study presents the design, implementation, and empirical evaluation of a locally deployable, knowledge-base-driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system in a customer service environment. In modern customer service systems, in addition to rapid response generation, particular importance is placed on professional accuracy, response consistency, and alignment with corporate communication principles. However, the application of general-purpose large language models is limited by the problem of hallucination and the lack of domain-specific knowledge. Although the adoption of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures has become increasingly widespread, only a limited number of studies have investigated their applicability in locally deployable, resource-conscious real-world enterprise environments. The proposed architecture incorporates the multilingual-e5 embedding model, the ChromaDB vector database, the BAAI bge-reranker-v2-m3 reranking component, and multiple locally deployed large language models (LLMs). During the empirical evaluation, several generator models and retrieval configurations were examined using 90 real customer service queries, resulting in the automated RAGAS-based analysis of 900 generated responses. The investigation also included the analysis of retrieval parameters, different retrieval configurations, and various document processing strategies. The experimental results demonstrated that the retrieval configuration, chunking strategy, and applied generator model all exert a significant influence on response relevance and factual consistency in resource-constrained local deployment environments. The findings also revealed that both the stability of the automated evaluation process and the response generation behavior of the models may vary substantially across different locally deployed models. Overall, locally deployable Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures can provide effective support for domain-specific customer service response generation tasks.
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Intelligent Systems and Informatics (SISY)

title: Evaluating chunking strategies across document types and their impact on RAG pipeline and AIagent performance
abstract: Izvleček: Generacija, podprta s pridobivanjem informacij (RAG), utemeljuje odgovore velikih jezikovnih modelov v zunanjih dokumentih, ki jih je treba pred iskanjem razdeliti na kose; način razdeljevanja je pomembna in premalo raziskana odločitev.Ta naloga sistematično in statistično utemeljeno primerja šest strategij razdeljevanja dokumentov (fiksna velikost, stavčno, pomensko, hierarhično, propozicijsko in kontekstualno) v štirih domenah (znanstveni članki, pravne pogodbe, prepisi sestankov in spletni članki), pri treh metodah pridobivanja, ponovnem rangiranju, dveh arhitekturah agentov in dveh modelih vektorskih vložitev -skupaj 132 nadzorovanih poskusov.Kakovost merimo z ogrodjem RAGAS in z jezikovnim modelom v vlogi ocenjevalca.Ker vse konfiguracije odgovarjajo na isti nabor vprašanj, primerjave opravimo na parnih razlikah po posameznih vprašanjih, z intervali zaupanja za samo razliko, permutacijskim testom in popravkom za večkratno testiranje.Rezultati tvorijo delno urejenost in ne enotne razvrstitve.Propozicijsko razdeljevanje je izrazito slabše od vseh drugih strategij, ker razčlenitev na atomarne trditve generatorju odvzame potrebni kontekst.Hierarhično razdeljevanje je statistično značilno boljše od stavčnega, pomenskega in razdeljevanja na kose fiksne velikosti, ne pa tudi od kontekstualnega, njegova prednost pa se pokaže pri tem, kaj cevovod pridobi, in ne pri kakovosti generiranih odgovorov; preostale štiri strategije so med seboj ekvivalentne v mejah 0,05 točke.Gosto in hibridno iskanje sta ekvivalentna in obe boljši od redkega iskanja BM25; ponovno rangiranje zamenja priklic za natančnost brez neto koristi; večkoračni agent redko iterira.Praktično priporočilo je pogojno: izberimo najcenejšo med zamenljivimi strategijami, razen kadar je merilo prav kakovost pridobivanja.
venue: Repository of the University of Primorsk (University of Primorska)

title: Knowledge Molecules in AI Knowledge Assistants: Task–State Boundary Certificates for Evidence Reuse
abstract: Retrieval-augmented AI assistants may reuse evidence after the task, provenance status, or source authority changes, making the boundary of a reusable knowledge item a con-sequential design decision. This study introduces a task–state boundary certificate for Knowledge Molecules (KMol): a verifiable contract linking a purpose-relative evidence wit-ness, an authority snapshot, and events that trigger revalidation. We formalize evidence ad-mission and counterfactual minimality as separate checks and evaluate them in reproducible finite-state simulations. Across 400 constructed cases, 1,600 task certificates were derived; a cross-task audit identified 3,900 decision mismatches among 4,800 reuse trials. In 11,200 source-event trials, reuse without revalidation produced 3,000 unjustified ALLOW decisions, which an event-aware verification gate prevented under the modeled rules. A further 2,400-update audit reduced rule-evaluator calls from 9,600 to 5,200 without missing modeled deci-sion changes; a matched generic dependency index tied KMol. A matched metadata-aware comparator achieved the same outcomes, locating the contribution in the explicit, auditable certificate protocol rather than a claim of superior prediction. The study provides operational definitions, executable algorithms, and testable validity conditions for evidence reuse in AI knowledge assistants. Independent source corpora and end-to-end generation are priorities for subsequent validation
venue: International Journal of Information Systems and Computer Sciences

title: AI-Generated Text Detection via Structural and Semantic Entropy Optimization with Adversarial Learning
abstract: AI-generated text detectors often achieve high in-domain accuracy but remain sensitive to changes in domain, generator, and writing style. This limitation partly arises because conventional detectors rely predominantly on latent language-model representations and fixed decision boundaries, without explicitly characterizing sample-level structural and semantic variation. We introduce S2E-AL, an end-to-end score-aware structure–semantic entropy adversarial learning framework for AI-generated text detection. S2E-AL encodes local dependency, global contextual, and semantic entropy features into a structure–semantic representation. A gradient-reversal source classifier discourages this representation from retaining source-specific information, while a score-aware threshold estimator conditions on both the entropy representation and a detached base-detector logit to produce a sample-specific logit adjustment. The adjusted logit is used to estimate the final probability that a text is AI-generated. Across HC3, HC3_Plus, LLMTrace, RAID, and XSum, the score-aware model achieved a macro Accuracy of 90.90% and a macro F1-score of 91.42%. Its performance remained lower on XSum, indicating that substantial domain and stylistic shifts remain challenging. These results suggest that jointly modeling structure–semantic variation and detector confidence can improve the overall performance–stability trade-off of AI-generated text detection across heterogeneous test distributions.
